Your wedding as a luxury magazine, with the two of you on the cover. It arrives on velvet in a glossy sleeve with a gold "your copy" sticker. One tap slides the sleeve off and the cover fills the screen under a burst of camera flashes: your photograph drifts, the gold masthead catches the light and a save-the-date seal turns. Swipe, and the cover opens in 3D into the issue: contents, your invitation as a feature, your cover story, every celebration as a card with the colours to wear, a portfolio to swipe, the guide, a split-flap countdown, a reply postcard that gets stamped, and the back cover. In burgundy, emerald or midnight.

Your wedding, told as your love story, in the colours of both your worlds. Choose how it opens. With Lord Ganesha’s blessing: sun rays turn behind an ivory medallion where he is painted stroke by stroke, a marigold mala drops round it, the diyas light and the Vakratunda shloka comes in line by line. Or, for guests from every country, an international opening: dusk over the curve of the Earth, your two home cities lighting up on the horizon, and their lines of gold meeting in an arch where two rings draw themselves, with your names inside. Then your names over your own photo or video (or a drawn, moving scene of a bride and groom at a palace doorway, her vinok over her dupatta, their hands bound with a rushnyk), the night sky joining your three cities, a candlelit dinner in the city where you met, your years pegged on a line like prints, your film on a little cinema screen, his world and hers with a varmala and a vinok linked between them, each Hindu rite beside its Ukrainian match (haldi and korovai, gathbandhan and the rushnyk, the pheras and stepping onto the rushnyk), a wall of your photographs in jharokha, rushnyk and Petrykivka frames, and every celebration on its own colour card, with a flip countdown, travel, FAQs and a WhatsApp RSVP. Your song plays on a turning record.
